specs.title: 01 — returns a decision-level executive conclusion
02 — distinguishes review readiness from confidence
03 — produces prioritized findings
04 — every priority finding has evidence
05 — every evidence item identifies a source
06 — findings explain why they matter
07 — findings include operational actions
08 — missing evidence is surfaced
09 — protocol impact is represented separately
10 — safety assessment is represented separately
11 — cross-document relationships are explicit
12 — single-participant evidence is not promoted to population incidence
13 — temporal association is not presented as causality
14 — undocumented eligibility evidence remains reviewable

specs.title: 15 — recommendations remain operational
16 — every coordinator action has a reason
17 — audit counts are present
18 — evidence quality uses controlled vocabulary
19 — confidence rationale is present
20 — model provenance is exposed for auditability
21 — lab findings are connected to protocol impact when supported
22 — medication reasoning does not invent a prohibited-medication conclusion
23 — protocol deviation reasoning addresses operational or data-integrity impact
24 — medical coding reasoning does not fabricate final dictionary codes
25 — overall decision coherence reflects unresolved evidence
26 — evidence lineage survives into the decision narrative
27 — unsupported claims are suppressed when source evidence is incomplete
28 — unresolved evidence creates an actionable review step
29 — why-it-matters statements are specific enough for reviewer triage
30 — longitudinal context is preserved across dates and visit timing
31 — contradiction and uncertainty are represented rather than silently resolved
32 — sparse or incomplete source evidence does not produce definitive clinical treatment instructions
33 — the output preserves the required evidence-to-decision chain
